Being a member of Capitol society in Panem is an honor not to be taken lightly, at least if you’re Drusilla Sickle, played by screen legend Glenn Close in “The Hunger Games: Sunrise on the Reaping.”

In the book, Drusilla is the cruel and vain escort for Haymitch Abernathy (Joseph Zada) and the rest of the District 12 tributes in the 50th Hunger Games, where she uses over-the-top fashion to broadcast her social status. Close worked closely with costume designer Bina Daigeler and hair, makeup and prosthetics designer Natalie MacGowan Spencer to ensure the character translated properly from Suzanne Collins’ bestselling prequel novel to the screen.

One challenge Daigeler faced was meeting Close’s request that each outfit felt connected, creating a through line that explained why Drusilla changes from one look to the next. Despite the drastic differences between each outfit, Daigeler established continuity through the character’s accessories, most notably a collection of gold medals and military-inspired epaulets that created a sense of authority.

“She wears all these medals, because somehow she thinks she is the top general of the capital,” Daigeler tells Variety.

And, not dissimilar to red-bottomed Louboutin shoes, Daigeler gave Drusilla dramatically long black nails that were painted red underneath to show her abundant wealth.

The character’s Capitol allegiance also went beyond her wardrobe, with Spencer overseeing her hair and makeup. While creating the looks, Spencer relied heavily on Collins’ source material to remain faithful to the author’s vision. Collins describes Drusilla as having implanted tabs that pull the skin on her face back, which Spencer wanted to honor. But because there wasn’t enough time each morning for an extensive prosthetics process, Spencer turned to Hollywood tape to tightly pull Close’s skin back, creating a distorted appearance. She later added tabs on the sides of Close’s face to complete the illusion, along with fake teeth that heightened Drusilla’s “scary” and “eerie” appearance.

“[Glenn] really wanted to pull it so taut that it changed all of her facial features, which it really did,” Spencer tells Variety.

Daigeler and Spencer’s shared mission: to create visuals that resonate with the franchise’s devoted fans — who “know their stuff inside out,” Spencer quips. “They’re so passionate.” When the book was released and casting announcements began rolling out, Spencer would regularly check social media to see what fans envisioned for the adaptation and what details they hoped to see on screen.

Below, Spencer and Daigeler break down the process of creating each of Drusilla’s costumes, hair and makeup, as well as the inspiration behind each look.

Drusilla makes her grand entrance at the District 12 reaping, wheeled into the frame wearing a bold yellow ensemble. The outfit is a stark contrast to the muted colors worn throughout Panem’s poorest district — the exact irony Spencer and Daigeler hoped to portray by making that the character’s brightest look in the film.

T-Mobile is getting an early start on the holiday shopping season, rolling out a slate of new deals on some of the year’s biggest smartphone releases, including Apple‘s new iPhone 18 Pro and its first-ever foldable phone, the iPhone Duo.

The wireless carrier is offering up to $1,200 off both devices with qualifying trade-ins on select plans, along with the option for eligible customers to walk away with a new phone for $0 upfront.

The device features a 5.4-inch exterior screen that unfolds into a 7.6-inch display — the largest ever on an iPhone — designed for watching videos, gaming and multitasking across apps. items.content:
内森·菲尔德 (Nathan Fielder) 和兰斯·奥本海姆 (Lance Oppenheim) 执导的伊丽莎白·霍姆斯 (Elizabeth Holmes) 电影《你可以看到一切》(You Can See Everything) 一直吸引着全国人民的关注，这是二十多年来第一部全球票房突破 1 亿美元的纪录片，可以说是美国电影作品中最具影响力、最多产的纪录片导演找到了新家。

As the nation remains enthralled by Nathan Fielder and Lance Oppenheim’s Elizabeth Holmes film “You Can See Everything,” the first documentary to cross $100 million at the global box office in over two decades, arguably the most influential — and the most prolific — documentarian in American cinema’s works have found a new home.

The complete works of Frederick Wiseman, the renowned documentary filmmaker behind “Titicut Follies” (1967), “Hospital” (1970) and “Ex Libris: The New York Public Library” (2017), have found a home with Janus Films. Wiseman produced, directed and edited 45 features that were released under Zipporah Films, Inc., his production and distribution company named for his wife, and they’ll all be distributed by Janus Films in North America starting Jan. 1, 2027, joining an impressive library that includes films by greats like Agnès Varda, Ingmar Bergman, Akira Kurosawa and Chantal Akerman.

Wiseman’s early films, from “Titicut Follies” (1967) through “State Legislature” (2007), will be available in 4K (having been restored by Zipporah Films), while “La Danse” (2009) through “Menus-Plaisirs — Les Troisgros” (2023) will be offered in their original digital formats. “A director whose rigorously objective explorations of social institutions constitute one of the most revered bodies of work in American documentary filmmaking,” according to The New York Times, Wiseman, who passed away earlier this year at the age of 96, crafted a one-of-a-kind filmography that chronicled the experiences of everyday people in the U.S. (and France). He was given the Honorary Award for lifetime achievement from the Academy of Motion Picture Arts and Sciences in 2016, and his works helped expose corruption in vulnerable communities.

“We couldn’t imagine a better home in North America for Frederick Wiseman’s films than with Janus Films,” said Karen Konicek of Zipporah Films. “It has been an honor to work alongside Fred for so many decades, producing and distributing his films. As Zipporah Films continues as the rights holder and distributor of the Wiseman Collection, we very much look forward to this new partnership with Janus Films and are excited to collaborate with them.”

“We are honored and thrilled to be the first distributor, in the U.S., outside of Zipporah Films, to be entrusted with licensing one of the greatest bodies of work in American cinema” said Peter Becker, President of Janus Films and Criterion. “We’re looking forward to presenting these monumental works, theatrically, to new audiences across the country.”

当被问及埃文斯对媒体的谨慎评论时，《世界末日》联合导演安东尼·罗素在故事中表示：“他非常致力于挽救电影院的体验。” “他说，‘我们为什么要妥协？’在所有参与其中的人中，就演员阵容而言，他可能是最致力于这方面的人。”

埃文斯还回忆起与漫威影业总裁凯文·费奇和联合总裁路易斯·德斯波西托共进晚餐，当时团队仍在拍摄《终局之战》。史蒂夫放弃美国队长头衔后的另一个身份——扮演游牧者的话题就出现了。

Chris Evans’ Marvel Cinematic Universe character Steve Rogers was written out of the franchise in 2019’s “Avengers: Endgame,” but the trailers for the upcoming “Avengers: Doomsday” have his return front and center.

In a new feature in Entertainment Weekly about “Doomsday,” the team behind the franchise reveals that Evans was never too far away — despite giving various interviews after “Endgame’s” release saying he was “happily retired” and “sad to not be back with the band.” In reality, Evans “took multiple meetings with Marvel in secret in the years following ‘Endgame.’”

“He’s very committed to saving the experience for the movie theater,” “Doomsday” co-director Anthony Russo said in the story when asked about Evans’ cagey comments to the press. “He’s like, ‘Why would we ever compromise that?’ Of anybody involved, as far as the cast goes, he may be the most committed to that aspect.”

Evans also recalled a dinner with Marvel Studios president Kevin Feige and co-president Louis D’Esposito while the team was still filming “Endgame.” The topic of playing Nomad, Steve’s alternate identity after giving up the Captain America title, came up.

“They said, ‘We’d love to continue making movies with you. Steve would no longer be Captain America, he would be Nomad,’” Evans said. “They sent me a pitch, and it was a great pitch. It really was. But for whatever reason at the time, I was very happy with how things wrapped up. It didn’t feel like it was the thing I was looking to do at the time.”

When audiences last saw Steve, he chose to travel back to the past to live a full life with his love, Peggy Carter (Hayley Atwell). At the end of “Endgame,” he appears in the present day as an old man to give the Captain America shield to Sam Wilson (Anthony Mackie). But in footage for “Doomsday,” Steve and Peggy look young again and have a child, so who knows what time shenanigans the movie has in store for audiences.

Watch the latest trailer for “Avengers: Doomsday,” which opens in theaters on Dec. 18.

该剧（12 月 1 日在音乐盒剧院首演）是截至 11 月 22 日当周百老汇演出最强劲的剧目之一，其他演出门票均售罄的还有《几个好人》、《汉密尔顿》、《无事生非》、《其他沙漠城市》，以及最后一周由比尔·欧文主演的《假想无效者》（票房收入 599,290 美元）。

票房收入最高的无疑是汉密尔顿，克里斯托弗·杰克逊 (Christopher Jackson) 重新饰演乔治·华盛顿 (George Washington)（截至 1 月 3 日），票房飙升至 3,039,502 美元。紧随其后的是“其他沙漠城市”，收入为 2,562,632 美元。接下来依次是《无事生非》（2,073,288 美元）、《狮子王》（1,936,616 美元）和《哈利·波特与被诅咒的孩子》（1,699,842 美元）。

Inter Alia, the previewing production of Suzie Miller’s new play starring Rosamund Pike, seems about to repeat its London success here on Broadway, with the first seven-performance week selling out and grossing $993,103.

The play (opening at the Music Box Theatre on December 1) was one of the stronger performers on Broadway for the week ending November 22, along with other sell-outs A Few Good Men, Hamilton, Much Ado About Nothing, Other Desert Cities and, in its final week, The Imaginary Invalid starring Bill Irwin (grossing $599,290).

Top earner was, far and away, Hamilton, with Christopher Jackson back in the role of George Washington (through January 3), sending box office soaring to $3,039,502. Closest runner up was Other Desert Cities at $2,562,632. Next, in order, were Much Ado About Nothing ($2,073,288), The Lion King ($1,936,616), and Harry Potter and the Cursed Child ($1,699,842).

Other Desert Cities, with Julia Louis-Dreyfuss leading a cast that includes Ed Harris, Allison Janney, Joe Keery and Lily Rabe, was, as usual, the priciest Broadway option, with an average ticket price of a whopping $328.88. The Fantasticks, at the Hayes in a production by the nonprofit Second Stage, grossed $375,151, filling 95% of the seats.

Hulu’s Reasonable Doubt has closed out its action-packed fourth season with a bloody good surprise: Kelly Rowland has joined the cast for Season 5. Jax and Krystal are stunned, replying, “Fuck!” simultaneously as the episode ends. A photo of the moment can be found above.

“After being such a fan of the show for such a long time, It’s surreal to be a part of it,” exclaimed Rowland.

Series creator, showrunner and executive producer Raamla Mohamed Hunter said of the cast addition, “Kelly Rowland, THEE Kelendria Rowland is in my show. The one I created. I didn’t think that I could bump like this, but now I have the motivation to be a survivor in this TV game. I’ll be screaming until Season five!”

Season 4 of Reasonable Doubt is about survival, truth, and rebuilding under pressure. Every character was forced to confront consequences they can no longer outrun as Jax’s fate hangs in the balance, driving the entire story forward in the new season.

With Jax’s most loyal client at the center of a spiraling media disaster, The Stewart Firm is thrust into a high-stakes battle where every move could mean survival … or collapse of the firm. As grief lingers and pressure mounts, one question looms: Can they rebuild in time, or will the cost of moving forward too quickly be everything they stand to lose?

James Marsden dominated social media buzz after Disney and Marvel Studios launched the final “Avengers: Doomsday” trailer, which ended on the viral moment of Marsden’s Cyclops uniting the X-Men and Avengers in battle against Robert Downey Jr.’s Doctor Doom. Marsden event got to recite his character’s iconic line: “To me, my X-Men!” Whether or not Marvel should’ve spoiled such a huge moment in the “Doomsday” trailer is now being widely debated among Marvel fans, but for Marsden it was moments like these that lured him back to playing Cyclops after 20 years.

“One of the things people have said for years is that Cyclops is a leader, yet in many of the previous films he often took a back seat to Wolverine and some of the other characters,” Marsden told Sharp magazine in a profile that published the same day as the “Doomsday” final trailer launch.

“There are only so many minutes available in a film this large, but it was important to me that my return felt meaningful,” he continued. “I didn’t want Cyclops to simply appear for a nostalgic cameo and then disappear. I wanted there to be a genuine purpose behind his presence. Without giving anything away, I feel very good about what we were able to do with the character.”

Marsden debuted as Scott Summers/Cyclops in 2000’s “X-Men” and reprised the role in 2003’s “X2: X-Men United” and 2006’s “X-Men: The Last Stand.” The character was killed off in the latter film, as Marsden moved on to film “Superman Returns.” But now Cyclops is back for “Doomsday” and leading the X-Men crew, which includes his original co-stars such as Patrick Stewart (Charles Xavier), Ian McKellen (Magneto), Kelsey Grammer (Beast), Alan Cumming (Nightcrawler) and Rebecca Romijn (Mystique).

Why did “Avengers: Doomsday” narrow in on these X-Men and not others such as Halle Berry’s Storm or Anna Paquin’s Rogue? Co-director Joe Russo recently told Entertainment Weekly the casting decisions were “really targeted. It was really specific.”

“We really do have a process where we see the entire film through each character’s eyes, no matter what the size of their role is,” Anthony Russo added.. “With the X-Men, we got to really deep dive and think about their histories as characters, their experiences, and how this particular moment in time was gonna affect them. There’s such a rich history to them that we really do bring them to the film as if it’s their movie, as well.”

“Avengers: Doomsday” opens in theaters Dec. 18.

Law firm Ropes and Gray aims to significantly raise its profile in Los Angeles and in the entertainment and sports arena with the hiring of the transactional legal team lead by Tom Ara and David Markman.

Ara and Markman are relocating to Ropes and Gray after having previously set up shop at Weil, Gotshal and Manges, which imploded earlier this month amid senior management turmoil and key departures. Also joining Ropes and Gray in Los Angeles with Ara and Markman is Max Offsay. In New York, David Yohai and Yehudah Buchweitz have joined Ropes and Gray as partners.

Ropes and Gray has about 1,500 attorneys spread across 16 offices worldwide.

“Everything we do at Ropes & Gray starts with our clients, and I’m thrilled to welcome nine extraordinary partners who share that conviction,” said Julie Jones, chair of Ropes & Gray. “We were intentional about adding partners who build on our client and practice strengths, help expand our global platform and who will thrive in the culture that makes Ropes & Gray the best partnership in elite law.”

Ara serves as head of the entertainment, sports and media group at Ropes and Gray, with Markman as partner. Ara and his team are known for handling high-level transactions across film, TV, music, sports, gaming and digital media. It also advises private equity sponsors, sovereign wealth funds, institutional investors on all manners of complicated commercial transactions.

Ara and his team joined Weil Gotshal in June 2025 after six years with DLA Piper.

items.content:
Netflix 自豪地成为了雷德福工作室中心的新主人，这座拥有 98 年历史的摄影棚综合体曾是《枪烟》、《玛丽·泰勒·摩尔秀》和《宋飞正传》的拍摄地。

该公司在一份声明中表示，该流媒体将于今天下午完成价值 3.8 亿美元的收购。该设施最后一次在 2021 年洛杉矶生产市场的高峰期以 18.5 亿美元的价格出售给 Hackman Capital Partners。随后产量的下降和利率的上升迫使哈克曼拖欠其 11 亿美元的贷款，并最终将财产转让给其贷款人高盛。

去年春天，Netflix 首次收购了斯蒂迪奥城这块 55 英亩的土地。高盛在周二的止赎拍卖中正式收回了该房产，这是与 Netflix 交易完成之前的最后一步。

此次收购标志着 Netflix 在洛杉矶的一项重大投资，该公司近年来也在新墨西哥州阿尔伯克基和新泽西州蒙茅斯堡进行了类似的投资。

items.originalContent:
Netflix is the proud new owner of Radford Studio Center, the 98-year-old soundstage complex that was home to “Gunsmoke,” “The Mary Tyler Moore Show,” and “Seinfeld.”

The streamer is set to close the $380 million acquisition this afternoon, the company said in a statement. The facility last sold to Hackman Capital Partners for $1.85 billion at the peak of the L.A. production market in 2021. The subsequent downturn in production volume and the rise in interest rates forced Hackman to default on its $1.1 billion loan, and ultimately to cede the property to its lender, Goldman Sachs.

Netflix first emerged as a buyer of the 55-acre site in Studio City last spring. Goldman formally took the property back at a foreclosure auction on Tuesday, the final step before the deal with Netflix could close.

The purchase marks a significant investment in Los Angeles for Netflix, which has made similar investments in Albuquerque, N.M., and Fort Monmouth, N.J., in recent years.

“There’s still a long way to go, but we are hopeful that with the partnership of the State of California and the City of Los Angeles, this will be the start of a meaningful new investment in California’s film industry,” the company said in a statement on Tuesday. “This city is home to us. We’re excited to keep investing here and finding more ways to entertain the world, while supporting the writers, builders, electricians, drivers, designers, and talent who make L.A., California, and the entertainment industry so special.”

Hackman Capital Partners proposed a $1 billion renovation of the aging Radford lot in 2023. Netflix is expected to continue that ongoing entitlement process with the city as it looks to preserve its development options and its ability to respond to market conditions.

Netflix has its L.A. office headquarters in Hollywood, and has no immediate plans to change that, as several years remain on its office leases. On top of the $380 million purchase price, Netflix also paid a 5.5% transfer tax due to the city’s Measure ULA.

Filming will proceed as usual on the lot. Cinelease will serve as the production equipment provider.

The horror satire “Namaslay” will be available to stream on Apple TV, Amazon, Fandango at Home and Google Pay on Dec. 15.

Directed by brothers Kanish Arhant-Sudhir and Rish Arhant-Sudhir, their feature film debut follows a grieving woman, Gayatri (Kirunthuja Srikanth-Talim), who is invited by her friend Judy (Angela Sant’Albano) to an upscale yoga studio to to reconnect with the yoga traditions she inherited from her late grandmother. The result is a fiery conversation about the appropriation of yoga in the West, proving culture is the blood that keeps the past alive.

“We’re thrilled to bring ‘Namaslay’ to an even wider audience through its digital release,” Rish and Kanish said in a statement. “We made this film to be experienced, shared and talked about and we’re excited that audiences across the country will have the opportunity to discover the world we created. As we continue our awards campaign, we’re grateful to everyone who has supported the film and look forward to its next chapter with audiences wherever they watch.”

To develop the meaningful story they wanted to share with audiences, the brothers turned inward to their real relationships and families’ lived experiences.

“There’s something that’s truly slapstick almost about the whole experience, but then there’s also something beneath that’s kind of sinister,” Rish said during the Variety Screening Series panel. “It’s a lot of strains of colonialism, there’s commoditization that’s happening, there is an extraction and then a resale at a premium.”

Kanish echoed, “An identity is not a story. It’s a part of a character that affects how they interact with a story, and there are a lot of movies that have characters who have various identities that are not palpable at all, but the identity of a character in and of itself is not enough to undergird a narrative.”

Alongside Srikanth-Talim and Sant’Albano, “Namaslay” stars Alicia Mitchell-Mangual, Usha Krishnan and Christina Moore. The film is produced by Venk Potula via Khrisp Entertainment, alongside producers Rish and Kanish through their independent film studio Junghal Studios.

items.content:
《穿越雪地》的导演卡尔森·杨发现，很容易将影片的两个主角瑞恩·米切尔（克里斯托弗·布尼饰）和汉娜·亨德里克斯（米歇尔·兰道夫饰）联系起来。

故事以两人为中心，两名高级编辑因即将裁员而竞相将对方赶下台，为他们所在的出版公司争取大笔图书交易。瑞安（Ryan）出于商业动机，利用流行的书籍来销售书籍，而汉娜（Hannah）则认为自己更像是一位文学纯粹主义者，她对自己所读书籍的深度进行了大幅调整。

“[剧本]真的对我产生了影响。我感觉自己与汉娜和瑞安的文学观点息息相关，感觉就像是我与自己进行的存在主义对话，时时刻刻，持续不断，”杨告诉Deadline。 “对我来说，了解他们的个性和内心世界很容易。然后我就喜欢随之而来的经典假日浪漫喜剧，我准备迎接挑战，尝试制作一部出色的假日浪漫喜剧。”

这位导演将对卖什么的不同立场与她在自己的工作中面临的挑战联系起来，“平衡艺术和商业，以及在讲故事和市场上什么是可行的，什么是不可行的。”

Clashing Through the Snow director Carlson Young found it easy to relate to the film’s two main characters, Ryan Mitchell (Christopher Briney) and Hannah Hendricks (Michelle Randolph).

The story centers the pair, two senior editors competing to oust the other from a condensed role due to impending layoffs, chasing big book deals for the publishing company where they work. Ryan operates off of commercial motivation and tapping into what is popular to sell books while Hannah identifies as more of a literary purist who takes big swings with the depth of books she takes on.

“[The script] really spoke to me. I felt so connected to Hannah and Ryan’s literary perspectives, and it felt like a existential conversation that I have with myself, moment to moment, constantly,” Young told Deadline. “It was easy for me to access their personalities and their inner worlds. And then I just loved the classic, holiday hijinks that ensue from there, and I was up for the challenge of trying to make a great holiday rom-com.”

The director connected the differing stances on what sells to challenges she navigates in her own job “balancing art and commerce, and what is and isn’t viable in storytelling and in the marketplace.”

RELATED: 7 New Christmas Movies Coming Out In 2026 From ‘Ebenezer’ To ‘Clashing Through The Snow’

“It is true that publishing and cinemas, these are tectonically shifting industries, and trying to find yourself your voice either as a book editor or director, whatever you’re doing, it doesn’t even need to be in a creative field,” she added. “But we’re all existing in these shifting sands, and so that was my way in. That’s why I was looking at it like that.”

In the below interview, Young unpacks specific moments like Lukas Gage’s “scene stealer” appearance, the Buc-ee’s knockoff Luc-ee’s, Ryan’s seeking advice by talking to ChatGPT and more.

DEADLINE: I spoke with Chris and Michelle earlier, and they mentioned you gave Chris a note comparing him to Jim Carrey. Did you have any other references? Could you expand on that?

CARLSON YOUNG: When we were rehearsing, I kept looking at him and seeing this physical comedy coming to the surface, and I was like, “This is like some Jim Carrey. I love this for you. Go off on that.” We tweaked it and trimmed it and shaped it in the edit, but he’s really funny. I hope that he does a lot more comedy.
